title: a seal names the extensionless file its proof loads by path
intention: A proof's seal names every repo file the proof executes by path, extensionless ones included, so an edit to any of them stales the seal.
why: Law 8: a seal an edit to its subject cannot expire is a quiet green that peers lean on. A seal over a proof that loads an extensionless repo file by path never names that file, so editing the file cannot stale the seal. 2026-11-20, eb2f8f9b0b8c: after bin/cmd/deletegate changed (82ab0b80a), the reseal-at-commit read test_delete_gate as 'settled red, closure unmoved' and did not rerun it; its fingerprint_closure was ['bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py'] alone. Two filters each drop the file: the exec audit hook ticket 6e50ed204abc added keeps only co_filename ending '.py' (cairn/devices/tester/device.py:112), and repo_relative_closure keeps only rel paths ending '.py' (cairn/tools/validation_store/validation_store.py:457). Scope, by a scan of every **/proofs/*.py: 56 proofs load by path (spec_from_file_location 45, SourceFileLoader 9, spec_from_loader 9, run_path 1, exec(compile 1); the 9 that load an extensionless file all use spec_from_loader(name, SourceFileLoader(name, path)) + exec_module, and are blind: bin/proofs/test_a_door_write_journaled_mid_pass_is_not_named.py (artifactgate); bin/proofs/test_a_record_path_refusal_names_every_way_out.py (artifactgate); bin/proofs/test_a_var_script_slot_runs_a_proof_only_through_its_loop.py (proofgate); bin/proofs/test_artifact_gate.py (artifactgate); bin/proofs/test_askscan.py (askscan); bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py (deletegate, trash); bin/proofs/test_probescan.py (probescan); bin/proofs/test_proof_gate.py (proofgate); cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_only_the_gate_writes_a_certificate.py (artifactgate). Read: the validations of test_delete_gate, test_artifact_gate, test_askscan, test_probescan, test_proof_gate each carry a one-entry closure (the proof).
how: In cairn/devices/tester/device.py, the exec audit hook keeps a code object's co_filename when it is a repo file, not only when it ends '.py' (an exec event is CODE being run, so a data read never enters). In cairn/tools/validation_store/validation_store.py, repo_relative_closure keeps an extensionless rel path that the run executed (e.g. bin/cmd/<name>), still dropping data files; the narrowest form keeps '.py' OR a file with no suffix. Proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_an_extensionless_module_loaded_by_path_is_in_the_seals_closure.py under PROVES this ticket's id, clauses 1-3, modelled on cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_module_loaded_by_path_is_in_the_seals_closure.py (a CAIRN_*_FIXTURE env re-run of itself that loads an extensionless tester-owned leaf by path). After the build, reseal the 9 blind proofs' validations so their closures name what they load.

clauses.claim: a fixture proof that loads an extensionless repo file through spec_from_loader(name, SourceFileLoader(name, path)) + exec_module, sealed through TesterDevice().run_proof, names that file in its fingerprint_closure, and the file's bytes are in sealed_fingerprint_now (the recorded number matches; the closure without it hashes differently)

live: bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py sealed by the built tester names bin/cmd/deletegate in its fingerprint_closure, and a one-byte edit to bin/cmd/deletegate makes that seal stale (sealed_fingerprint_now differs) with no explicit --seal; the same holds for each of the 9 proofs in the measured blind set, each naming the extensionless file(s) it loads

the narrowing stays code-only: a file the fixture only READS as data (a .json, a .md, opened with open()) is not in its closure, and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_module_loaded_by_path_is_in_the_seals_closure.py stays green

a fixture proof that only RUNS an extensionless repo file as a subprocess (sys.executable <file>, never loading it in-process) names that file in its fingerprint_closure — the reach log already records it as the child's __main__ __file__, and repo_relative_closure must keep it

decisions.text: D1: the exec audit hook keeps executed repo files with no suffix as well as .py.
D2: repo_relative_closure keeps executed no-suffix repo files as well as .py; this alone also closes the subprocess-run case via the reach log (clause 4).

D3: the proof plus validation, one tooth per clause (1-4), modelled on the prior art. The fixture is a committed extensionless, stdlib-only leaf at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/fixtures/extensionless_leaf, exiting through raise SystemExit like every python bin/cmd script.

measured.saw: the missing_check measured: subprocess-run is blind by the SAME second filter, not a different mechanism. A scratch fixture proof in bin/proofs that only ran bin/cmd/deletegate as a subprocess, sealed through TesterDevice().run_proof: closure ['<the proof>'] alone. Re-sealed with only repo_relative_closure patched to also keep executed no-suffix repo files: closure ['bin/cmd/deletegate', '<the proof>'] — reach/sitecustomize.py logs every module __file__ unfiltered, so the reach log already carried it, and nothing else entered
measured.how: worktree /var/tmp/wt-b7d5 at 069a9e356, probe bin/proofs/_probe_subprocess_only_gate.py (never committed) driven by two run_proof seals, unpatched then with filter #2 monkeypatched

measured.saw: building clause 4: a subprocess-run script that falls off its last line is NOT in the reach log, extensionless or .py alike — CPython 3.14 pops __main__.__file__ after the script completes, so reach/sitecustomize.py's atexit reads None; a script ending in raise SystemExit keeps __file__ and is logged. Every python bin/cmd script (28 git files) exits through SystemExit/sys.exit, so clause 4 holds for the gates; the normal-end case is a separate mechanism, ticketed apart, not a clause here. Built worktree: clauses 1, 3, 4 green, clause 2 red until the 9 reseal; build reverted: 1, 2, 4 red, 3 green
measured.how: python3 /var/tmp/noext_probe (atexit prints __main__.__file__ -> None) vs /var/tmp/noext_probe2 (raise SystemExit(0) -> the path); the proof run in /var/tmp/wt-b7d5 with and without the two filter edits
